pr_title: [GR-31840] [GR-31681] Allow native-image shared libs to be built on module-path and fix resource bundle lookup.
pr_body:
- Removes the undocumented native-image.properties property `ImageIncludeBuiltinModules`. It was previously needed for building truffle-based images. Cleaning up class-init for Java 11+ make the existence of  `ImageIncludeBuiltinModules` obsolete. (I.e. if there is truffle, it's classes are subject to class-init)
- Fix implementation of ResourceBundle access. Packages that contain ResourceBundles are opened up in their respective modules prior to accessing them from the image-builder. This also fixes https://github.com/oracle/graal/issues/3404
- Add support for building shared library images where the `--module-path` is used.
- Build native-image-agent and native-image-diagnostics-agent via `--module-path` and test the shared objects in `mx hellomodule`

**Describe the issue**

Bundles included in JDK 16 are not discovered and can't be included in the native image.

I have an application that declares the following in `resource-config.json`:

```json
{
  "resources": {
    "includes": []
  },
  "bundles": [
    {"name": "com.sun.org.apache.xerces.internal.impl.xpath.regex.message"},
    {"name": "com.sun.org.apache.xerces.internal.impl.msg.DatatypeMessages"},
    {"name": "com.sun.org.apache.xerces.internal.impl.msg.DOMMessages"},
    {"name": "com.sun.org.apache.xerces.internal.impl.msg.JAXPValidationMessages"},
    {"name": "com.sun.org.apache.xerces.internal.impl.msg.SAXMessages"},
    {"name": "com.sun.org.apache.xerces.internal.impl.msg.XIncludeMessages"},
    {"name": "com.sun.org.apache.xerces.internal.impl.msg.XMLMessages"},
    {"name": "com.sun.org.apache.xerces.internal.impl.msg.XMLSchemaMessages"},
    {"name": "com.sun.org.apache.xerces.internal.impl.msg.XMLSerializerMessages"},
```

@ilopmar See the following in the [JDK 16 Release Notes](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/javase/16-relnotes.html#JDK-8256299):
> JEP 396: Strongly Encapsulate JDK Internals by Default
Strongly encapsulate all internal elements of the JDK by default, except for critical internal APIs such as sun.misc.Unsafe. Allow end users to choose the relaxed strong encapsulation that has been the default since JDK 9.
>
> With this change, the default value of the launcher option --illegal-access is now deny rather than permit. As a consequence, existing code that uses most internal classes, methods, or fields of the JDK will fail to run. Such code can be made to run on JDK 16 by specifying --illegal-access=permit. That option will, however, be removed in a future release.

Due to this change, the `java.xml` module that contains these bundles is no longer opened to all unnamed modules by default, which is why Java applications can no longer use these bundles without additional configuration options. So, unless the options for building an image are different from ones for running an application, I would say that this is not a bug.

@pejovica Thanks for the explanation.

Thank you. Please let me know if you need help with that app that reproduces the problem :-)

I was able to reproduce the problem and this is indeed a bug on our side. Specifically, in the Micronaut-Liquibase integration test, these bundles are accessed from within the `java.xml` module, which is why everything works on the JVM. However, during image building, the image builder tries to access these bundles from the outside (i.e., from an unnamed module) and fails because it does not have the required access.

So, until we have a proper solution, you will need additional JVM arguments when building the native image as a workaround. You can use `-J--add-opens=...` as you already figured out, or you can use `-J--illegal-access=permit` instead.

@ivan-ristovic this is the issue we were talking about today. This needs the builder-specific opening up of private packages where a given ResourceBundle is located in (see `substratevm/src/com.oracle.svm.util.jdk11/src/com/oracle/svm/util/ModuleSupport.java`). Once we have that, also `com.oracle.svm.util.ModuleSupport#getResourceBundleFallback` should become obsolete (so we can delete it).

Hi @ilopmar I finally have a decent fix for this issue. It will allow you to use your original `resource-config.json` as is.

In addition I will also add support for disambiguating ResourceBundle names in case the same fully qualified bundle name exists in more than one module.

Suppose there is a bundle named `some.random.qualified.BundleName` in module `foo.a` and `foo.b`. Using
```
{"name": "foo.a:some.random.qualified.BundleName"},
```
will then allow you to specify that you only want the one from module `foo.a`. If the bundle would be requested without module qualification both bundles will end up in the image.
Great news! Once your PR gets merged I'll try it again with my app.
Thanks @olpaw, tried with our Micronaut-Liquibase test application and it works as expected :-)

review_comments: Clever idea to allow the user to specify the module from which the bundle should be loaded. However, I would put the parsing into the caller and have the module as an optional argument. For the command-line options, it makes sense to have this parsing, but for the config file, a new key-value pair separate from the bundle name might be more expressive. And the classloader support shouldn't be aware of the nuances of locale configuration parsing. However, this is more of a `todo` for me to implement it once this gets merged.

> Clever idea to allow the user to specify the module from which the bundle should be loaded.

Thanks. The idea is actually from @ilopmar https://github.com/oracle/graal/issues/3404#issuecomment-839888673

Hi @olpaw ,

With this check in place jar files including resource bundles in .properties file format at their root are not supported. Such an example is [org.eclipse.yasson](https://github.com/eclipse-ee4j/yasson/tree/master/src/main/resources) (seen failing in https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/18305).

Going through [ResourceBundle's Javadoc](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/api/java.base/java/util/ResourceBundle.html) I was not able to find any mention/guidance on avoiding adding ResourceBundles to the root of jar files, so I am wondering if this is something we should relax on GraalVM.

Thanks
